1990: Docker beta; 2000: LXC; 2005: Solaris Zones; 2010: Kubernetes first stable version
2005: OpenVZ; 2008: Docker alpha; 2010: LXC; 2013: Kubernetes first public release
1976: IBM LPAR; 2013: Docker; 2015: LXC; 2016: Kubernetes reaches stable version

64dfcf42820c.domanda: What does Docker use to implement the Overlay network between containers on different hosts in Swarm?
64dfcf42820c.spiegazione: The Overlay network allows containers to communicate across different nodes as if they were on the same LAN. The underlying technology is VXLAN (Virtual eXtensible LAN): it takes an Ethernet frame and encapsulates it in UDP/IP, which traverses standard IP networks. At the destination node, it is decapsulated and delivered. Containers see a flat virtual Ethernet network. VXLAN extends VLANs from 4096 IDs to 16 million virtual IDs.
risposte: The BGP protocol to create dynamic routing between Docker host nodes in the cluster
VXLAN: encapsulates Ethernet frames in UDP/IP packets, traversing standard IP networks
GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnel over IPv6 between Swarm cluster nodes
IPsec to create end-to-end encrypted VPNs between all Docker Swarm cluster nodes

25a99468dbe8.domanda: What does `docker exec -it mycontainer bash` do?
25a99468dbe8.spiegazione: `docker exec` runs a command in an already running container — it does not create a new one. `-i` (interactive) keeps stdin open; `-t` (tty) allocates a pseudo-terminal: together they enable interaction. `mycontainer` is the target. `bash` is the command. Result: a shell inside the container for navigating the filesystem, inspecting processes, reading logs, modifying configurations. If bash is not available, use `sh`. Essential for troubleshooting.
risposte: Creates a new container based on the 'mycontainer' image and starts bash in interactive mode
Stops the 'mycontainer' container and opens a bash shell to inspect post-mortem logs
Runs bash in the already active 'mycontainer', in interactive mode (-it): opens a debug shell
Copies the log files of 'mycontainer' to a bash directory on the host filesystem

80faff9963db.domanda: Which consensus algorithm does Docker Swarm use among manager nodes?
80faff9963db.spiegazione: Docker Swarm uses Raft for consensus among managers. It ensures that all managers agree on the cluster state (services, replicas, nodes). It tolerates (N-1)/2 failed managers: with 3 managers → 1 failure, with 5 → 2 failures. A Leader manages decisions; the others are Followers. If the Leader fails, Raft automatically elects a new Leader. Kubernetes uses etcd (also Raft) for the same purpose.
risposte: Paxos — the most widely used distributed consensus algorithm in classic enterprise systems
PBFT (Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance) — used in Swarm to tolerate malicious nodes
Round-robin — managers take turns making decisions without a true consensus algorithm
Raft — distributed consensus, tolerates (N-1)/2 failed managers

cbad1404dd3d.domanda: What does the `compose.yaml` file contain in a Docker Compose project?
cbad1404dd3d.spiegazione: The `compose.yaml` (formerly `docker-compose.yml`) defines the multi-container application in YAML. Sections: `services` (each service is a container with image, ports, env, volumes, dependencies via `depends_on`), `volumes` (volume definitions), `networks` (virtual networks). With `docker compose up -d` Docker starts all containers. With `docker compose down` it stops them. It should be versioned in Git to reproduce the application anywhere.
risposte: Definition of the multi-container application in YAML: services (images, ports, volumes, env), volumes, and networks
Instructions for building the Docker image, equivalent to the Dockerfile in YAML format instead of free text
The list of system environment variables of the host on which the Docker daemon runs
The configuration of the Docker daemon (dockerd) for the host operating system

9624bfcd2aad.domanda: What is the default tag of a Docker image if nothing is specified?
risposte: `stable` — identifies the latest stable version certified by the project maintainer
`latest` — used automatically if no tag is specified
`v1` — later versions are called v2, v3 in ascending order
The build date in YYYYMMDD format, automatically generated by Docker at pull time
9624bfcd2aad.spiegazione: Docker images follow `[registry/][utente/]nome[:tag]`. Without a tag, Docker uses `:latest`. Examples: `nginx` = `nginx:latest`; `ubuntu:22.04` specifies the version. WARNING: `latest` does not necessarily mean 'the most recent'; it is just the default tag, and a maintainer may not update it. In production, always use a specific tag (e.g. `nginx:1.25.3`) for reproducibility and to prevent breaking changes.

64db8fc77bd1.domanda: What does `docker compose down` do compared to `docker compose stop`?
64db8fc77bd1.spiegazione: `stop`: sends SIGTERM and stops the containers — they remain stopped and can be restarted with `start`. The containers still exist with their writable layer. `down`: stops AND removes containers and networks created by Compose. Data in volumes is preserved by default (to remove them: `down -v`). After `down`, you need `up` to restart (recreates from scratch). `stop` = pause; `down` = cleanup (to update the compose.yaml).
risposte: They are identical: both stop and remove containers, networks, and volumes of the project
`stop` stops the containers without removing them; `down` stops AND removes containers and networks (volumes are preserved)
`down` only stops the containers; `stop` also removes the Docker images associated with the project in compose.yaml
`stop` is deprecated and no longer works in recent versions of Docker Compose

5133d48e3095.domanda: What does `docker logs mycontainer` do and when is it useful?
5133d48e3095.spiegazione: `docker logs mycontainer` displays the output (stdout and stderr) of the container's main process. Docker automatically captures stdout/stderr. Options: `-f` or `--follow` (live, like tail -f), `--tail N` (last N lines), `--since 1h` (filter by time). It is the first debugging tool: if a container crashes, the reason is usually in the logs. No need to enter with `exec`.
risposte: Shows the list of all containers that used the same image as 'mycontainer'
Exports the logs of 'mycontainer' to a file on the host filesystem in /var/log/docker/
Displays stdout and stderr of the container's main process, useful for debugging without exec
Lists all commands executed by the root user inside the active 'mycontainer' container

b78fe84859ff.domanda: What is a Docker Volume and how does it differ from a bind mount?
b78fe84859ff.spiegazione: Docker Volume: managed by Docker in /var/lib/docker/volumes/, lifecycle independent of the container, survives `docker rm`, shareable between containers, manageable with `docker volume`. Bind mount: maps a host directory (e.g., /home/user/data) into the container. More direct and flexible for local development (you modify the code on the host and the container sees it), but depends on the specific host path.
risposte: The Volume is temporary and is deleted with the container; the bind mount is persistent and survives
The Volume works only on Linux; the bind mount works natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux
The Volume is used only in production with Swarm; the bind mount only in individual local development
Volume = managed by Docker in /var/lib/docker/volumes/; bind mount = host directory

a442088a39f9.domanda: What is the typical structure of an OpenTofu/Terraform project?
a442088a39f9.spiegazione: Standard structure: `main.tf` (resources: containers, VMs, networks, storage); `provider.tf` (providers, e.g., Docker, Azure, with credentials); `variables.tf` (input variables: name, type, default); `outputs.tf` (exported values post-apply: IP, URL); `versions.tf` (OpenTofu and provider versions); `.gitignore` (excludes .terraform/, *.tfstate). Plus a descriptive `README.md`.
risposte: main.tf (resources), provider.tf (providers), variables.tf (inputs), outputs.tf (outputs), versions.tf (versions)
app.tf (application), infra.tf (infrastructure), config.tf (configurations), deploy.tf (deployment), monitor.tf (apply monitoring)
index.tf (entry point), modules/ (modules), state/ (state), secrets/ (credentials), README.tf
main.yaml (resources), provider.json (providers), Dockerfile (image), compose.yaml, .env

bd0ac4dd1d1e.domanda: Why is Ansible considered a 'procedural' IaC tool compared to Terraform?
bd0ac4dd1d1e.spiegazione: Ansible uses YAML playbooks with sequential tasks: 'Step 1: install nginx', 'Step 2: copy config', 'Step 3: start service'. Procedural = HOW. Terraform/OpenTofu is declarative: 'I want nginx configured like this', and determines the operations autonomously. Ansible can cause errors on the second run if not idempotent; Terraform is idempotent by design. In practice, they are used together: Terraform for infrastructure, Ansible for OS/apps.
risposte: Because it uses XML instead of YAML for application playbook configuration files
Because it works only on Windows machines and not on modern Linux/Unix systems
In playbooks, sequential tasks (install, configure, start) are written instead of the desired final state
Because it does not maintain a state file like Terraform and therefore does not know what has already been created previously

8dafafd267a3.domanda: What is OpenTofu and how did it originate in relation to Terraform?
8dafafd267a3.spiegazione: Terraform by HashiCorp was MPL (Mozilla Public License), open source. In 2023, HashiCorp switched to BSL (Business Source License), which is more restrictive (prohibits commercial use by competitors). The community forked it: OpenTofu, adopted by the Linux Foundation as an independent and genuinely open-source project (MPL). Compatible with Terraform: same HCL, same providers, same syntax. Commands: `tofu init/plan/apply/destroy`.
risposte: Google project created from scratch to directly compete with HashiCorp's Terraform in the cloud market
Open-source fork of Terraform after HashiCorp's license change; managed by the Linux Foundation
Paid enterprise version of Terraform with inclusive commercial support from HashiCorp
Separate tool that uses a different language than HCL, compatible only with native Kubernetes

2e53aad3214e.domanda: In the OpenTofu Azure provider, why is the `features {}` block mandatory even if empty?
2e53aad3214e.spiegazione: In the OpenTofu/Terraform azurerm provider, the `features {}` block is syntactically mandatory even if empty. The minimal configuration is: `provider "azurerm" { features {} }`. Without it, `tofu init` or `tofu plan` will result in a validation error. It is used to configure optional behaviors (e.g., what to do when deleting a resource group), but it must be present even with default settings. This is a specific syntactic detail that often causes errors for beginners.
risposte: It is only an optional stylistic convention: the code works fine without it
The `features {}` block enables experimental features of OpenTofu specific to Azure
The block specifies the Azure API version to use to ensure backward compatibility
It is required by the azurerm provider specification: without it, a configuration error occurs

e9614f598987.domanda: What does `tofu destroy` do and when should it be used with caution?
e9614f598987.spiegazione: `tofu destroy` is the most dangerous command: it reads the tfstate, identifies all managed resources, and deletes them from the real infrastructure — VMs, containers, networks, storage, everything. It shows the plan and asks for confirmation ('yes'). In production: extreme caution is required, as deletion is irreversible (unbacked-up data is lost). Use cases: cleanup of test/staging environments, teardown of temporary infrastructures, laboratory environments.
risposte: Deletes only local HCL configuration files without touching the client's real infrastructure
Shows a destruction plan without executing anything, equivalent to `tofu plan -destroy`
Resets the terraform.tfstate file back to its initial empty project state
Deletes all real managed resources (VMs, containers, networks); irreversible, caution in prod

74902ca817f8.domanda: What does the presence of multiple Availability Zones (AZs) within an AWS Region ensure?
74902ca817f8.spiegazione: Each Region contains 2-6 AZs. Each AZ consists of one or more physically separate data centers within the same geographic area, featuring independent power, cooling, and connectivity. They are interconnected via a high-speed, low-latency network (<1ms). They are isolated from failures in other AZs: an incident like a fire, flood, or power outage in one AZ does not impact the others. Distributing an application across multiple AZs ensures high availability.
risposte: Ensures that resources are distributed across different countries to comply with GDPR
Redundancy: AZs are separate data centers in the same area, isolated from failures in other AZs
Ensures lower prices for EC2 instances due to internal competition between AZs
Ensures that each AZ is managed by a different hosting provider to avoid vendor lock-in

739e19ea2a4f.domanda: What is a Security Group in AWS and how does it differ from a Network ACL?
739e19ea2a4f.spiegazione: AWS provides two firewall levels in VPC. Security Group: at the EC2 instance (or ENI) level. STATEFUL: if you allow inbound TCP on port 80, the outbound response is automatic. Network ACL: at the subnet level. STATELESS: explicit rules for both inbound and outbound. Rules are numbered and evaluated in order. SG = first line of defense; NACL = additional layer.
risposte: The Security Group is an IAM user group; the Network ACL is a subnet-level firewall
They are identical: both filter traffic at the single EC2 instance level in the same way
Security Group = stateful, applied to the EC2 instance; Network ACL = stateless, applied to the subnet
The Security Group is applied to VPC subnets; the Network ACL is applied to individual EC2 instances

ee28bf5c4845.domanda: What are the three main public cloud providers and how do they position themselves in the market?
ee28bf5c4845.spiegazione: The three main cloud providers: (1) AWS (Amazon Web Services) #1, since 2006, with the broadest catalog; (2) Microsoft Azure #2, with strong integration into the Microsoft ecosystem (Office 365, AD, Windows Server), preferred by enterprises already using Microsoft; (3) Google Cloud Platform (GCP) #3, particularly strong in AI/ML (TensorFlow, Vertex AI), Big Data (BigQuery), and Kubernetes (Google created K8s). The market is growing; AWS is the leader, while Azure and GCP are gaining market share.
risposte: AWS (#1), Microsoft Azure (#2, Microsoft ecosystem), Google Cloud (#3, AI/ML)
Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud — respectively #1, #2 and #3 globally
AWS (#1), Google Cloud (#2), Alibaba Cloud (#3): Azure is outside the top 3
Microsoft Azure (#1), AWS (#2), Google Cloud (#3): Azure surpassed AWS in 2022

3d6f1c76aeba.domanda: How does AWS handle Black Friday traffic spikes without downtime?
3d6f1c76aeba.spiegazione: The Black Friday case study demonstrates 'rapid elasticity'. Physical servers: supporting 50x traffic would require purchasing thousands of machines used for only a few hours a year—an enormous waste. AWS solves this with elasticity: the Nitro Hypervisor starts a VM in 5-10 seconds. At midnight on Black Friday, auto-scaling detects the spike. Within seconds, the number of VMs scales from 200 to 600 to 3000 automatically. When traffic subsides, the VMs are terminated. You pay per use for the actual seconds consumed. Result: 0 downtime, costs proportional to usage.
risposte: By pre-purchasing additional physical servers every September to be shut down in January of the following year
By limiting the number of simultaneous accesses with a virtual queue system during spikes
Nitro Hypervisor starts VMs in 5-10s; auto-scaling scales from hundreds to thousands of VMs and terminates them when traffic drops
By using dedicated Black Friday data centers that remain off the rest of the year and are only turned on in November for the spikes

ed16e1f4cc85.domanda: What is the key lesson from the Netflix case study on cloud migration?
ed16e1f4cc85.spiegazione: The Netflix case study encapsulates the cloud's promise. Before (2008): physical servers → DB corruption → 3 days offline → 9.39M subscribers. After AWS: every server is a VM (replaceable), evening peaks handled with auto-scaling, zero hardware. In 2016, Netflix shut down its last physical data center. Today, it serves over 300M subscribers on AWS. Lesson: the cloud is not just about cost, but about agility, reliability, and focus on core business.
risposte: The cloud is always cheaper than on-premise in any possible business scenario
Physical servers are always preferable to the cloud for high-traffic workloads like streaming
Netflix uses AWS only for backup; streaming still runs on proprietary physical servers
Cloud = HA, instant scaling, focus on the product: Netflix serves over 300M subscribers on AWS

d2b9089b77c6.domanda: What does `git status` do and when should it be used in the daily workflow?
d2b9089b77c6.spiegazione: `git status` is the orientation command for the Git workflow. It should be used before `git add` and `git commit`. It shows: files in red (modified but not staged — working directory), in green (staged — ready for commit), and untracked (new). IaC workflow: `git status` (what has changed?) → `git add .` → `git commit -m '...'` → `git push`.
risposte: Shows the complete history of all repository commits with author, date, and message
Synchronizes the local repository with the remote by downloading all available latest changes
Shows the status of the working directory and staging area: modified, staged, untracked
Checks the connection with the remote repository and shows whether a push is possible at this moment

b4726972c651.domanda: What does `git log --oneline` do, and what information does it show?
risposte: Shows the commit history in compact form: abbreviated hash (7 characters) + message, from the most recent
Shows the list of files modified in the repository's last commit, in compact form, one line each
Shows only the current user's commits, excluding those of the project's collaborators
Exports the repository history to a text file formatted for external documentation
b4726972c651.spiegazione: `git log --oneline` shows the history in compact form: abbreviated hash (7 characters, unique) + the commit message, from the most recent. Example: `a3f8c21 Versione B: container CON volume`. Without `--oneline` it shows the full hash (40 characters), author, date and the extended message. Useful for finding a commit's hash before `git checkout <hash>` to return to that version.

46901e09d4bb.domanda: What does `git push -u origin main` do and what does the `-u` flag mean?
46901e09d4bb.spiegazione: `git push origin main` pushes the local main branch to the remote repository 'origin'. The `-u` flag (= `--set-upstream`) sets up tracking: the local main branch 'follows' the remote one. After the first push with `-u`, subsequent pushes are simply `git push` without specifying. The tracking is stored in the local config. Without `-u`, you must always write `git push origin main`.
risposte: Downloads ('pull') the main branch from the remote origin to the local repository with a forced update
Publishes the main branch to origin; `-u` links the local branch to the remote for future pushes
Deletes the main branch from the remote origin and also removes it from the local repository
Merges the main branch with the current branch and then publishes it to origin

f591d3b15492.domanda: What does `git branch` do, and what does the asterisk (*) in the output indicate?
risposte: Lists the configured remote repositories; the asterisk indicates the main remote (origin)
Lists the local branches; the asterisk indicates the current branch (where HEAD points)
Creates a new branch with the specified name; the asterisk is a wildcard for multiple names
Deletes all branches except the one with the asterisk, which is kept as the project's main branch
f591d3b15492.spiegazione: `git branch` without arguments lists the local branches. The asterisk (*) indicates the current branch — where HEAD points. Example: `* main` / `feature-login` / `bugfix-volume`. Related commands: `git branch nuovobranch` (creates), `git branch -d nome` (deletes), `git branch -M main` (renames). In the IaC workflow, after `git checkout HEAD~1` the asterisk shows 'detached HEAD'.

c9309b856723.domanda: What is 'packaged' software and how does it differ from 'custom' software?
c9309b856723.spiegazione: Packaged Software: a standard product from a vendor sold/licensed to many customers. Examples: SAP ERP, Microsoft Office, Salesforce. Advantages: ready-to-use, low initial cost, vendor support, updates. Disadvantage: the company adapts its processes to the software. Custom Software: developed for a company's specific processes. Advantages: perfect fit, competitive advantage. Disadvantages: high cost, long development times, internal maintenance.
risposte: Packaged = packaged in a Docker image; Custom = installed directly on the OS without containers
Packaged = developed specifically for a particular company; Custom = standard product sold with a commercial license
There is no difference: both refer to commercial software with a paid proprietary license
Packaged = standard product (SAP, Office) for many customers; Custom = developed for a single company

37acf0c872d0.domanda: AWS Lambda is an example of which cloud computing paradigm?
37acf0c872d0.spiegazione: AWS Lambda is the most well-known FaaS service, the emblem of Serverless. Model: you write a function (Python, Node.js, Java...), upload it to Lambda, and configure the trigger (HTTP via API Gateway, S3 upload, SQS message, CloudWatch event). When the trigger fires, Lambda executes, returns the result, and terminates. Cost per millisecond: if it is not invoked, the cost is zero. Automatic scaling to thousands of parallel executions without configuration.
risposte: IaaS: provides virtual VMs on which to run custom code with manual operator scaling
PaaS: provides a managed platform for continuous deployment of complete web applications
SaaS: is a ready-to-use application without the need for the user to write additional code
FaaS / Serverless: executes functions in response to events, pay per ms, automatic scaling

0a260442d0c9.domanda: What is the primary immediate benefit of virtualization in a data center?
0a260442d0c9.spiegazione: Consolidation is the most immediate benefit. Before: each app on a dedicated server to avoid interference → average utilization 10-15% (85-90% wasted). With virtualization: multiple VMs (each with its own app) on the same physical server with guaranteed resources. A modern server hosts 20-50 VMs. Benefits: fewer servers to buy, less rack space, less energy, less cooling, less hardware to maintain. Typical ratios 10:1 or higher.
risposte: Server consolidation: multiple VMs per physical host, fewer machines, rack space, energy, costs
Complete elimination of downtime thanks to live migration of VMs between different hosts in the cluster
Automatic performance increase of a single application thanks to the hypervisor
Total elimination of the need for backups thanks to automatic VM snapshots

d2e6d82d7214.domanda: What is the difference between an optical disc (CD/DVD/Blu-ray) and an HDD?
d2e6d82d7214.spiegazione: Optical discs (CD, DVD, Blu-ray) use a laser to read/write on reflective polycarbonate layers. This technology differs from HDDs (magnetism) and SSDs (NAND flash). Advantages of optical discs: portability, durability, low unit cost. Disadvantages: limited capacity (Blu-ray up to 100 GB), slow access, fragility. Historical use: software/music/video distribution, archiving. Today replaced by downloads and cloud, still used in some archives.
risposte: The optical disc uses rotating magnets like the HDD but with higher density; both for primary storage
Optical disc = laser on reflective layers (distribution/archiving); HDD = magnetic heads on rotating platters
There is no real technological difference: modern DVDs use the same magnetic technology as HDDs
The optical disc uses NAND flash like SSDs but in a removable format; the HDD uses magnetic platters

a2b1506bb5bf.domanda: What is a Container Service in Docker Swarm and how does it differ from a single container?
a2b1506bb5bf.spiegazione: In Swarm, a Service is the scalable deployment unit. It defines: image, number of replicas (e.g., 5 instances), update policy (rolling update without downtime), load balancing among replicas, and restart on crash. Swarm decides on which nodes to run the replicas, detects crashes and restarts them, and distributes traffic. Definition in `compose.yaml` with the `deploy` section. It is the abstraction for horizontally scaling microservices.
risposte: Single Docker container with a custom name and automatic restart policy in case of crash
The dockerd process running on each worker node of the Swarm cluster in production
The private registry service integrated in Docker Swarm for internal Docker images
Set of replicas of the same container with load balancing, scaling, and automatic restarts

a679061a8b02.domanda: What is idempotency in IaC and why is it a fundamental property?
a679061a8b02.spiegazione: Idempotency is a mathematical property: applying an operation multiple times produces the same result. In declarative IaC: if you run `tofu apply` 10 times without modifying the code, after the first apply (which creates/modifies), subsequent runs do nothing because desired state = actual state. It is fundamental for reliability: you can re-run without fear of duplicating resources. Non-idempotent shell scripts and Ansible playbooks tend to produce errors on the second execution.
risposte: Applying the same IaC code multiple times always produces the same final result, without accumulated effects
It means that IaC can be written in any programming language without differences in the final result
It means that IaC can be executed by any user without special administrative permissions
It means that IaC code is identical across different cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) automatically
